analysis:
The PR changes only CHANGELOG.md, which is documentation. It renames the v0.10.2 candidate heading to a published release and adds a v0.10.3 candidate section (head lines 11-25). The section describes a fix for an M5 crash in the MLX attention_nax_dsplit kernel. It also lists submodule pin moves: libs/mlx-swift from eedca444 to 4926d3d9, and libs/mlx and the nested mlx from ff4bb35b to 31f550af. The actual submodule pin changes are not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify them.

I found no change to executable code, authorization, attestation, encryption, cache storage or coordinator contracts. I also found no weakening of existing controls.

The security-relevant statements I checked:
- Watchdog auto-update on crash: this relies on the existing T-043 mechanism, in which the watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable provider binary. The text does not alter that mechanism.
- The KV-backend guard binds to the version that tripped it and clears on upgrade. This is a stated behavior, not a change visible here.
- The text says nothing else changes from 0.10.2. It also does not touch T-041 prefix-cache properties.

No threat-model update appears needed from this documentation diff alone.

Remaining question for later passes: if the real PR also bumps the MLX submodule pins, the pinned MLX Metal kernel changes should be reviewed. That review is outside the supplied units and the evidence given.
